findings.obs_text: In Pro 14:15 the simple believes everything while the prudent gives thought to his steps: believing without weighing is set against thought. In Rom 12:3 sober thinking of oneself is by the measure of faith God gives. In Phili 3:4 and Jam 1:26 a person thinks he has reason for confidence or is religious: the thought is a self-trust the verse tests. In Heb 11:11 faith goes with the conceiving.
findings.grounds: the prudent gives thought to his steps

findings.obs_text: In 2Sa 5:6 the Jebusites say the blind and lame will ward David off, thinking he cannot come in: blind is part of their boast, which their thought rests on.
findings.grounds: the blind and the lame will ward you off

findings.obs_text: In 2Cor 11:16 and 2Cor 12:6 thinking is how others rate Paul, and boasting is what he weighs doing: let no one count him a fool, and he refrains from boasting so that no one thinks more of him than he sees.
findings.grounds: let no one think me foolish

findings.obs_text: In 1Sa 18:17 Saul asks David to be valiant while he thinks to let the Philistines kill him: the call to courage hides the thought. In Job 32:6 Elihu was timid to declare his opinion. In Pro 21:29 the wicked puts on a bold face while the upright gives thought to his ways.
findings.grounds: A wicked man puts on a bold face

older.finding: Fear holds back from speaking: "Samuel was afraid to tell the vision to Eli"; the servants "were afraid to tell him that the child was dead"; Elihu "was timid and afraid to declare my opinion"
